model: Aurora HydroLink2 for TruClimate 100 / TruClimate 500 Modular Chillers
equipment_type: Modular chiller / water-to-water heat pump controller
applies_to: WaterFurnace TruClimate 100 dual scroll (NXW) and TruClimate 500 modular chillers with the Aurora HydroLink2 controller, including 4-pipe and 6-pipe header rack builds and variable speed modules.
summary: BACnet objects of the Aurora HydroLink2 controller used on TruClimate 100 dual scroll and TruClimate 500 modular water-to-water chillers. It covers system enable and emergency shutdown, aquastat, setpoint or network control of the compressors, variable speed capacity control, load and source water temperatures and limits, per-compressor refrigerant data, and header rack valve and loop control. Each row is ticked for the configurations it applies to.
notes: The workbook file is version 3.04, but its title row still reads version 3.01.
Writable points are marked with the BACnet priorities they accept (in1, in4, in5, in8, in16); they are shown here as commandable (C). Points marked 'no' are read-only.

Columns tick each point for 12 configurations: NXW dual scroll, modular dual scroll and modular variable speed (no header rack, 4-pipe standard or reversing, 6-pipe standard or dedicated source) and dual screw. Header rack and variable speed points only exist on those builds.
Successor of the HydroLink v1.03 list (PL2500EW): all 213 of its objects appear here with the same instance and name, and 89 were added for modular, variable speed and header rack builds.
MSV 3 option 4 names AV 12 as the network temperature, while AV 62 is described as the network temperature input.
The sheet does not state the BACnet transport or network settings.

integration.summary: For units without a header rack, choose aquastat, setpoint, network or setpoint-with-enable control on MSV 2. In setpoint mode the controller holds AV 22/23 against the input picked on MSV 3; in network mode the BAS calls compressor A on BV 35 and B on BV 34, and variable speed systems can take capacity targets on AV 306/307 when BV 301/302 are enabled. Keep BV 37 Enabled and set BV 36 to Network while the BAS has control.

minimum_points.name: SystemEnable_c
minimum_points.why: System enable; compressors stay off when Disabled

minimum_points.name: NetworkControl_c
minimum_points.why: Set to Network while the BAS has control

minimum_points.name: AlarmReset_c
minimum_points.why: Alarm reset; return to Normal after the lockout clears

minimum_points.name: SystemStatus_st
minimum_points.why: Overall status: normal, alarm, shutdown, load shed...

integration.enable: BV 37 SystemEnable_c (default Enabled) must be Enabled for the compressors to run. The BAS sets BV 36 NetworkControl_c to Network when it takes control. With MSV 2 = 3 (Network), BV 35 and BV 34 call compressors A and B and BV 1 picks cool or heat. BV 2 EmShutdown_c forces an emergency shutdown.
integration.remote_sensors: AV 62 NetworkTemperature_c is the BAS-supplied control temperature for setpoint control on a network temperature (MSV 3 option 4). Header rack builds take BAS cold and hot water temperatures on AV 506/507 (MSV 502/503 option 4) and network loop temperatures on AV 508 and AV 510-515.
gotchas: BV 5 EnableManualOverride_c lets BV 6-8 override compressor and reversing valve outputs; normal logic keeps running underneath.
BV 0 lead/lag enable is kept for compatibility; the sheet says BV 42 replaces it to avoid instance 0 problems.
Header rack mode comes from AV 568 or MSV 501, chosen by BV 511.
With BV 502 Active, all header rack valves follow their manual values.
Check the configuration columns in the source: many points only exist on some builds.
